A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Finite Difference Flow Optimization for RL Post-Training of Text-to-Image Models. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original post-training experiments, Flow-GRPO comparisons, ablations, qualitative outputs, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a live human-feedback training demonstration and an expanded baseline comparison.

M1.justification: The paired-trajectory update, stochastic sampler, normalization, clipping, and Algorithms 1-4 are unchanged. The human-feedback experiment supplies a different reward source to the existing method; no revised optimization procedure is specified.

E1.justification: Section 5.6 adds an actual live human-preference training scenario using HPDv2 prompts. HPDv2 already appeared in v1's evaluation, so this extends feedback and interaction coverage without introducing a new prompt benchmark or generation domain.

E2.justification: The new Appendix A comparison and Figure 17 substantially expand beyond Flow-GRPO to ReFL, DDPO, online/offline DPO, online/offline SFT, and offline reward-weighted regression. These methods have reported comparison curves, rather than merely new citations.

E3.justification: New protocols include one author labeling 3,200 on-policy image pairs across 50 training rounds over approximately four hours. Figure 17 compares methods by generated training-image count, with counts estimated from training steps for ReFL and DDPO. Existing experimental settings and evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and Figures 10 and 16 add a qualitative case study of whether direct human feedback can steer generation within a short training session. Existing component ablations, stochasticity analyses, CFG comparisons, and KL-regularization analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing seed and multiple-image sampling descriptions are unchanged. Neither addition introduces repeated-training-run statistics, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the approximate image-count caveat concerns comparison protocol rather than statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 17 adds substantial comparator result curves, while Figures 10 and 16 add human-feedback training outcomes. Appendix A reports PickScore 23.76 at 400,000 generated images and a 0.61 gap over Online Flow-DPO with beta=100. Existing numerical results and plotted curves are retained; these additions do not establish a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The sampler derivations, mathematical assumptions, and Appendix C analysis connecting finite differences to a smoothed reward gradient are unchanged. Equations and theoretical arguments are retained despite pagination changes.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims that the method's simplicity and data efficiency enable training with on-policy human preferences. The abstract, conclusion, and central claims about faster convergence and higher-quality generation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.6 newly attributes practical human-feedback training to sample efficiency, pairwise updates, and support for non-differentiable rewards. Appendix A characterizes the PickScore comparison as a conservative case for the method's gains, while Figure 17 qualifies the ReFL/DDPO comparisons as approximate.

D1.justification: v2 documents the human experiment's generate-label-train workflow, single-author live labeling, approximate four-hour duration, and absence of reward models or offline preference data. The existing implementation details, hyperparameter tables, hardware measurements, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5.6 explicitly positions the demonstrated on-policy human-feedback approach against Diffusion DPO's pre-collected preference data, and Appendix A broadens empirical positioning across post-training families. The cited-work set is unchanged; publication and access-date updates are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.6, two Appendix A paragraphs, and brief introduction and results-overview edits. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained, with updated cross-references and limited bibliographic editing.

P2.justification: v2 adds two human-training image figures and one baseline-comparison plot, Figures 10, 16, and 17. Existing figures and tables are retained, with renumbering, relocation, and page reflow rather than substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparison strengthens empirical context, and the live human-feedback prototype provides concrete evidence for an application previously left undemonstrated. The gains are limited by qualitative evidence from one author and approximate image-count normalization for ReFL/DDPO; the existing method, theory, and principal results remain unchanged.
